prompt: A glass paperweight is a pyramid with a square base $6$ cm on each side and a height of $10$ cm. What is its volume?

hints.text: Take a third: $360 \div 3 = 120$ cubic cm. Choice B.

explanation: The base is a square: $6^2 = 36$ square centimeters.
A box with that base and height $10$ would hold $360$ cubic cm.
A pyramid holds one third of that: $V = 120$ cubic centimeters. Choice B.

alternativeExplanations.title: Why choice D is so tempting
steps: $360$ is the volume of the BOX around the pyramid — what you get by forgetting the $\frac{1}{3}$.
A pyramid tapers to a point, so it obviously holds less than the box it fits inside. Any pointed solid (cone or pyramid) carries that $\frac{1}{3}$.
